 Tulum Flight Collapse: Only 2 US Routes Will Remain By February
 By: Author The Cancun Sun 
 Posted on Published: November 10, 2026 
 1 Comment 
 Share The Article 
 Facebook 
 X 
 Email 
 When the brand new Tulum International Airport officially opened its doors, it was hailed as a massive game changer for travelers heading to the Mexican Caribbean. Instead of landing in Cancun and taking a 2 hour highway shuttle down the coast, tourists could finally fly directly into the jungle. It sounded like the absolute perfect travel hack. However, just a short time into operations, the reality of flying into this specific destination is looking incredibly different. The massive wave of direct flights from the United States is rapidly drying up.
 Airlines are pulling back hard, and the flight map is shrinking fast. If you are planning a winter escape to the trendy beach town this year, your direct options are going to be incredibly limited. By the time February 2027 rolls around, there will only be 2 nonstop United States routes left standing.
 The Only 2 Surviving US Routes
 Major carriers spent the last few months quietly slashing their direct Tulum schedules. United Airlines is completely ending its direct services from Houston and Newark. American Airlines is also pulling the plug on its secondary route out of Miami. All of these massive cuts will be completely finalized by the 1st week of January 2027.
 Once the dust settles, American travelers will only have 2 options to reach Tulum without a layover. American Airlines will continue operating 1 daily flight out of Dallas Fort Worth. Delta Air Lines will keep its direct connection from Atlanta running every single day except Tuesdays and Wednesdays. If you do not live near those 2 specific hub cities, you are going back to booking flights into Cancun and taking the bus.
 Why Are US Airlines Bailing?
 You might be wondering how an incredibly popular beach town is suddenly losing its direct flights. The reality goes much deeper than just being too close to the massive Cancun airport. The Tulum tourism industry is currently facing a massive collapse driven by extreme, out of control pricing. Local businesses tried to forcefully transition a rugged backpacker destination into a luxury hotspot with prices comparable to Miami, but completely failed to upgrade the actual infrastructure to match those premium rates. Tourists are simply refusing to pay wildly inflated prices for transport, hotels and restaurants.
 This massive pricing problem bleeds directly into the new airport experience. Aviation consultant José Suárez Valdés points out that getting out of the Tulum terminal is a massive financial trap for arriving travelers.
 “The complementary services offered in Tulum are much more expensive,” Suárez Valdés stated. “I’m talking about taxis, perhaps ride-hailing services, or the possibility of not being able to use a ride-hailing service… 3rd party services developed by the airport are much more complicated and expensive.”
 Travelers are doing the math and realizing that booking a cheaper flight into Cancun and grabbing a shared shuttle is still significantly cheaper than flying directly into Tulum and getting price gouged by a local taxi. Because of this massive price difference, statistics show the Tulum airport actually lost almost 45 percent of its passengers between January and August. Airlines are seeing these empty seats, realizing the expensive Tulum bubble has burst, and immediately pulling their planes out of the market.
 Canada Saves The Winter Season
 While United States carriers are aggressively retreating, the airport is not turning into a total ghost town. The Canadian market is stepping up heavily to anchor the international terminal this winter. Unlike the United States flights that completely disappear in early January, Canadian airlines built a massive seasonal schedule designed to ride out the entire winter and spring break travel rush.
 If you are flying from Canada, you have 6 incredibly solid nonstop routes that will continue operating all the way through mid April 2027. Travelers leaving from Toronto can catch a weekly Sunday flight on Air Canada running through April 11, or fly WestJet on Thursdays and Saturdays until April 24. If you are departing from Montreal, Air Canada flies every Thursday until April 8, while Air Transat runs a Sunday route through April 18. Calgary flyers get 2 weekly flights on WestJet operating on Thursdays and Saturdays all the way through April. Finally, Air Transat is keeping a weekly Sunday flight open for travelers coming out of Quebec City for the exact same duration.
 The Real Future Of The Jungle Airport
 So what exactly happens to this massive new infrastructure project? It is simply settling into a much more realistic role. It was never actually going to replace Cancun. Instead, it is slowly shifting into a secondary airport strictly dedicated to low cost carriers and seasonal vacation flights.
 Budget airlines like Viva Aerobus and Mexicana de Aviacion are absolutely thriving here, offering extremely cheap domestic hops. When you combine those budget carriers with the massive wave of seasonal Canadian flights, the airport still has a highly functional purpose. It is just not the massive luxury United States hub everyone originally predicted. If you want to fly direct from the United States this winter, you better book those Dallas or Atlanta routes right now before the few remaining seats are completely sold out.
